source.title: Weight-Sharing Regularization
source.authors: Mehran Shakerinava; Motahareh Sohrabi; Siamak Ravanbakhsh; Simon Lacoste-Julien

record.file_problem: Full paper text provided, including experiments and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether explicit weight-sharing regularization changes held-out accuracy and the train–test gap, including comparisons across architectures and datasets. Its intervention differs from the claim versions’ original experiments.
record.gate_note: Rows capture test-accuracy outcomes and prediction asymmetry reported for regularized and comparator networks. The paper does not test random-label memorization, width scaling, optimizer choice, batch size, dropout, sharpness measures, or example removal. CIFAR10 table reports test accuracy and weight-sharing/sparsity metrics but no training accuracy there.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out accuracy of convolutional and fully connected networks trained from scratch, testing V3 on augmented CIFAR10 and translated or shuffled MNIST. It is not an original source for V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that proximal weight-sharing regularization improves MLP generalization in a low-data setting and yields convolution-like filters. The invariant CNN performs best on unshuffled torus MNIST and retains its advantage when only locality is destroyed; the regularized MLP performs best when permutation also violates the CNN's translation symmetry. They describe the results as preliminary.
record.recipe_differences: Uses proximal-gradient weight-sharing regularization and compares fully connected networks with CNNs; does not reproduce the original convolutional-versus-fully-connected studies' methods or full settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset structure and whether CNN symmetry assumptions match the data; training-data ratio is varied in Figure 5, with the text stating the benefit is especially apparent at reduced ratios.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2024), PMLR Volume 238
record.problems: The authors report no error bars. For the cited test-accuracy results, training accuracy is not reported for each CIFAR10 model in the supplied text. The MNIST table gives a single test-accuracy result per model.
record.rows_left_out: No table rows omitted. Figure 5 dataset-ratio-specific test-accuracy values are not extracted because the supplied text describes the trend but does not state the individual values; the figure is not used to infer exact numbers.

untested.parts: Fitting fixed random labels and comparing natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Width scaling beyond the width needed for zero training error.
CIFAR-100 and SVHN; initialization of fully connected networks from trained CNNs; a controlled attribution of the CIFAR10 advantage to learned local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of optimizer tuning.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and retraining.

missing.what: Condition-specific MLP comparisons for both shuffled datasets: plain MLP 92.40%, MLP + ℓ1 93.57%, and MLP + R 95.04%. The text explicitly states these accuracies are unchanged. These rows establish the architectural ranking under each permutation condition.

record.verdict_notes: Table 2's CNN variants denote dataset transformations, not modified CNN architectures. The original MNIST limits_scope rationale was insufficient: improving an MLP while the CNN remains better supports the architectural ranking. The actual qualifications concern locality's small contribution and reversal under incompatible symmetry. No error bars are reported.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence are not tested.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.

The study compares a CNN and fully connected networks, including weight-sharing regularization, on MNIST on a torus and CIFAR10; it does not test all listed datasets or the sparse-local-connection and convolutional-initialization conditions.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
